Key ratios, the change from last year, and the place among peers

Source: R/xbrl_ratios.R
xbrl_ratios.Rd

Takes a panel from xbrl_panel() and adds what an analysis reads off it: the ratios the statistics offices publish, how each company moved since its previous filing, and where it stands among comparable companies the same year.

Usage

xbrl_ratios(p, group = "class", min_peers = 5)

Arguments

p

A panel from xbrl_panel().

group

Columns of p that make companies comparable. Default "class".

min_peers

Smallest group a median and a rank are computed for. Default 5.

Value

p with the ratios, the changes and the peer columns added.

The ratios

The definitions are the statistics offices', not corporate finance's, so that a figure here can be set beside a published one:

  • equity_ratio – equity / assets (soliditetsgrad).

  • return_on_assets – profit after tax / assets (afkastningsgrad, as Statistics Greenland publishes it).

  • operating_return – operating profit / assets: the return before interest and tax, which is what a company's operation earns on what it has.

  • return_on_equity – profit / equity, NA where equity is not positive.

  • operating_margin – operating profit / revenue (overskudsgrad); operating_share_of_gross the same against the gross profit, which is what a class B filing has.

  • current_ratio – current assets / short-term debt (likviditetsgrad); cash_ratio cash / short-term debt.

  • debt_ratio – debt other than provisions / assets; shortterm_debt_share short-term debt / assets.

  • interest_coverage – operating profit / finance expenses.

  • staff_share – staff costs / gross profit (lonkvote). The gross profit of a Danish filing is revenue less goods and external costs, which is value added at factor cost, so value_added is it.

  • value_added_per_employee, profit_per_employee.

A ratio whose denominator is missing, nought, or of the wrong sign for the ratio to mean anything is NA.

The change from last year

For a company with a filing for the year before – its previous period ending 11 to 13 months earlier – gross_profit_growth, revenue_growth, assets_growth and equity_growth are the relative changes and equity_ratio_change is the change in percentage points. A company whose previous figure was not positive has no growth rate, because a change from a loss is not a percentage.

Among peers

group names the panel's columns that make companies comparable. The default is the accounting class, because that is in every filing. A branch of industry is a better comparison and is not in a filing: join it to the panel on cvr and name its column here. For each group and year, the median of equity_ratio, operating_return, current_ratio and return_on_equity is added, with each company's percentile rank among its peers (*_pct, 0 to 100). A group with fewer than min_peers companies gets neither: a median of three companies is mostly one company's figure.

See also

xbrl_panel(), and xbrl_robustness() for how vulnerable a company is.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
p <- xbrl_panel(read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl"))
r <- xbrl_ratios(p)
r[c("cvr", "period_end", "equity_ratio", "equity_ratio_pct")]

# against a branch of industry from a register extract of your own
p$branch <- register$branch[match(p$cvr, register$cvr)]
r <- xbrl_ratios(p, group = "branch")
} # }
